examShortTricks: Trick 1: Classification by hydrolysis: cannot hydrolyse = mono; two units = di (sucrose = glucose+fructose, maltose = glucose+glucose, lactose = glucose+galactose); many = poly (starch, cellulose).
Trick 2: Glucose evidence chain: C6H12O6, reduces Tollens/Fehling (aldehyde), pentaacetate → 5 OH, CN addition → 6C (chain), no mutarotation-free... quote 3–4 reactions for the structure proof.
Trick 3: Sucrose is NON-reducing (both anomeric carbons bonded, glycosidic α,β-1,2) and is called invert sugar on hydrolysis (rotation +66.5° → −20°).
Trick 4: Starch (α-glucose, helical, iodine blue) vs cellulose (β-glucose, straight chains, H-bonded, not digested by humans — no cellulase).
